originality.rationale: Theorem 2.1 and Section 3 of Barak-Pelleg and Berend give expectations for the projective-plane mechanisms, not all-time stochastic comparisons. The derived exact Fano tail gap and the complete q=3 sign reversal are not consequences of their expectation inequality; the q=3 example explicitly shows why a mean comparison cannot certify stochastic order. General recovery-set techniques can calculate finite distributions, but do not directly imply the strict all-time sign pattern here. value.rationale: The exact first-order stochastic comparison is a natural strengthening of the 2026 finite-geometric counterexample to expected coverage-time extremality. The Fano mechanism is slower at every nontrivial tail, but the very next projective-plane mechanism reverses direction between t=4 and t=5. The sharp discrete sign classification distinguishes global mean delay from transient rapid completion; it is a structural boundary for natural benchmark designs, not a routine new parameter value.
